subtitle: Pitch-Aware Resonant Shimmer
tagline: A scale-aligned filter bank finds the musical resonances inside a sound and feeds only those into an octave-up crystal grain loop.

body.lead: TB Jewel Digger & Finder picks out the harmonic "jewels" in a sound. A filter bank tuned to a base note and scale isolates musical resonances, a motion engine moves them in time, and a crystal grain loop turns them into a shimmering layer, an octave up by default.

body.p: Unlike a reverb that washes over everything, the shimmer grows only from the notes you select, so it stays in key with the music. Use it on pads, guitars, piano, vocal tails, field recordings, and ambience.

ul: Scale-aligned band-pass filters: base note C0–C8, ten scales, density up to 24 bands
Two filter modes: FIND lifts the chosen bands, DIG carves into them
Six Shovel materials that change the resonant character
Ten motion types, free rate or tempo-synced divisions, motion depth, and randomness
Crystal grain loop with size, pitch, envelope, delay, feedback, damping, spread, and reverse chance
Crystal Only mode, low cut, mix, and output
Display of the filter response on a note scale

steps: Scale, Motion, Base Note → target pitches
FIND or DIG band-pass filters (Q, density)

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Jewel Digger & Finder 1.3.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.0.2 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert the plug-in on a pad, guitar, piano, or ambience track.
Set `Base Note` {{3}} and `Scale` {{4}} to the key of the music.
Keep `Amount` and `Q` {{6}} low at first, then raise them until the chosen notes stand out.
Choose a `Motion` type and set `Rate` {{7}}; start slow.
Raise `Crystal Mix` and `Crystal Send` in CRYSTALLIZING {{9}} to grow the shimmer layer.

body.p: The filter bank places band-pass filters on the notes of the chosen scale, starting from Base Note. FIND lifts those bands so the chosen notes ring out; DIG cuts into them for a carved, inverted character.

rows: The root note of the filter bank.

note.text: Synced motion follows the host tempo between 20 and 320 BPM.

body.p: The crystal stage is a grain delay loop that receives the filtered notes, pitches them (an octave up by default), and feeds them back to build a shimmering layer above the source.

rows: How much of the filtered signal enters the crystal loop.
Level of the crystal layer in the output.
Pitch of the grains. +12 st is one octave up.
Grain fade-in, shown in milliseconds (42 ms at the default Size).
Grain fade-out, shown in milliseconds (78 ms at the default Size).
How much of the crystal output is fed back. High values build long, growing tails; the loop is soft-clipped to stay controlled.
High-frequency damping in the loop. Higher values give darker, softer tails.
Stereo spread of the crystal layer.

Turns off the filter path so only the crystal layer is heard.

Keeps the low end out of the processed signal.

warn.text: High Feedback with long Delay and Size can build up a lot of energy and raise peaks and CPU load. The crystal loop has a fixed buffer of about ten seconds.

body.p: Choose a preset from the PRESET list, step through factory presets, or use LOAD USER PRESET... to open a .tbjewel file. Save stores the current settings. The list shows CUSTOM after you edit a preset; Undo and Redo step through changes.
Factory presets: **Initialize**, **Harmonic Lantern**, **Amber Drill**, **Frozen Constellation**, **Phase Dust**, **Reverse Shards**, **Octave Rain**, **Cathedral Shimmer**, and **Fifth Halo**.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: In-key shimmer on a pad
recipes.use: A glowing octave layer that follows the harmony.
steps: Raise Feedback slowly until the tail sustains between chords.

recipes.title: Arpeggiated resonances
recipes.use: Rhythmic, pitched sparkle from a sustained sound.
steps: Lower Density for clearer, more separate notes.

recipes.title: Fifth-interval halo
recipes.use: An open, harmonically rich layer above guitars or piano.
steps: Check that the layer stays in key with the chords.

recipes.title: Reverse crystal texture
recipes.use: Backwards, glassy grains for ambience and transitions.
steps: Blend back with Mix if the texture should sit under the source.

rows: The shimmer clashes with the music.
Set Base Note and Scale to the key of the song, or use Still motion.
Switch on Low Cut, or raise the Base Note.
Lower Feedback, shorten Delay, or raise Damp.
The filter sounds too thin or whistling.
Lower Q or Amount, or switch from Dig to Find.
It is used only by Motion types that include randomness.
Synced motion does not follow the song.
Make sure Sync is on and the host is playing; tempos outside 20–320 BPM are clamped.
